hero.title: Stop shipping the page everyone has already seen
hero.line: A very honest skill that stops your agent from shipping that generic UI junk.

references.sectionLabel: Real sites from the galleries the skill names
references.region: Canvas of real sites. Drag or use the arrow keys to look around; open a card to see it large.
references.alt: The first screen of {name} ({host}), captured at 1440 by 900.
references.copiedImage: Image copied. Paste it into your agent chat.
references.prompt: Use the attached screenshot of {name} ({host}) as a layout reference. What it shows: {use}. Take its spacing scale, type hierarchy (sizes, weights, line lengths) and grid. Do not copy its text, images, logo, colors or brand. Map what you take onto this project's DESIGN.md tokens, and say which parts you used.

use.augen: One image, lots of white space
use.obys-format: Display type as the whole hero
use.vercel: Split hero with a logo row

catalog.title: Every tell comes with a fix
catalog.body: Read straight from the skill. A tell is allowed only when your DESIGN.md makes it the brand.

gallery.title: The newer tells
gallery.wordsAlt: A generic SaaS landing page with each newer tell outlined and tagged: label-above-headline, em-dash-density, pulsing-dot, big-number-row, section-numbering and side-stripe.
gallery.iconsAlt: Close-up of a six-card feature grid, each card with a purple icon tile, side stripe, generic marketing lines, and a View more link, tagged icon-soup, generic-cta, and side-tab-border. The right column is clipped.
gallery.loopsAlt: Close-up of a cyber dashboard: a CYBER. wordmark tagged period-logo, an All systems online badge with a pulsing green dot tagged attention-loop, and a bouncing INITIALIZE_ button tagged bounce-easing.
gallery.placeholdersAlt: Close-up of a poorly composed hero: a centered slogan, cheap flat SVG blob illustrations at uneven angles tagged svg-placeholder, and soft purple blur orbs tagged blur-blob.
gallery.wordsBody: Tiny label on top of every fucking headline. Em dash every which way. Copy that goes “Not X. A Y.” and tells the user nothing. Trash all of it and write copy that actually looks good.
gallery.iconsTitle: Slop cards nobody can stand anymore
gallery.iconsBody: Lightning, rocket, sparkle icons on every damn card, and those side strips nobody can stand anymore — someone had to say it. Oh, and those 10 identical CTAs on the same screen? Your user is exhausted just looking at it.
gallery.loopsBody: A button that never gets tired of bouncing. A status dot blinking for no reason. Congrats, you’re the world’s best motion designer — except you’re not. Let’s clean up this mess by doing the basics well.
gallery.placeholdersTitle: Ugly SVGs you somehow think look good
gallery.placeholdersBody: Enough of those hideous flat SVG illustrations on your site. That isn’t illustration, it’s an abomination. Grab some references and prompt your generative AI for real images — not this SVG trash.

install.title: Pick your agent, install it in one line

commands.title: Let's fix this dumpster fire of a site
commands.exReview: /antiwebslop review this page and tell me everything that’s slop.
commands.exBuild: /antiwebslop build a new hero section for me, no slop.
commands.exGeneric: /antiwebslop this looks like every generic SaaS landing out there. Make it look like real design.
commands.exPlaywright: /antiwebslop open this page and run visual QA at the main breakpoints with Playwright, then tell me what broke.
commands.exGuidelines: /antiwebslop audit my UI against Vercel’s web-interface-guidelines. Report findings as file:line.
commands.exImageToCode: /antiwebslop use image-to-code to help me make something close to this reference image I sent you.
commands.exReference: /antiwebslop I pasted a reference. Use it to guide the design of this page.

eval.title: How the skill is measured
eval.intro: Each run is scored out of 42 for slop absence, craft and process. Scope safety is a gate: if the run changes product UI the brief didn't ask for, it fails, whatever its score.
eval.runTitle: Let each run finish on its own
eval.setupShort: Same agent, model and brief in two clean checkouts. The skill is installed in one only.
eval.runShort: Each run finishes on its own: no steering, one scripted follow-up, lint and screenshots saved.
eval.blindShort: Someone else hides which is which. The reviewer picks one, then scores both on the 42-point card.
eval.decideShort: Ship only at 1.3× the baseline, with zero lint errors and a blind win or tie in 2 of 3 briefs.

footer.tagline: A design skill, a lint, and an eval kit for web pages built by AI coding agents.
